{{Top}}
{{Quote|You don't realize how important a datapad is until you're stranded on Raxus Prime with nothing but your boots and a blaster.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="NEGWT">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Datapad-SS.png|300px|thumb|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker's]] datapad in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]]]]

A '''datapad''' was a small, usually low-cost, electronic device used for storing information. Taking the place of the more primitive [[Book/Legends|book]], a datapad could store textual, graphic, and [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] data. They were commonly used as notebooks, day planners, calculators, and sketchpads. Some models could interface with and download information from larger computer networks. Most datapads came standard equipped with a touch-sensitive color screen, [[Audio sensor|audio pickups]], headphone ports, and [[Power cell/Legends|power packs]].

==Description and usage==
[[File:Clone_using_a_datapad.png|thumb|172x172px|left|A clone trooper using a model of datapad used by the Confederacy of Independent Systems and Galactic Republic]]
Datapads were small, handheld [[Computer/Legends|computers]] that were used for data gathering and storage and could download information from larger networks when interfaced directly with it. Capable of being customized to run specialized programming, datapads were generally used for organizing and recording information. Datapads served multiple functions, including as notebooks, day planners, calculators, and sketchpads. Datapads commonly weighed around three [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]], and cost around a thousand [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].<ref name="RPG-Core">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook]]''</ref>

[[MicroData Technologies/Legends|MicroData Technologies]] were one of the corporations that manufactured datapads,<ref name="EGWT">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> offering a wide range of other datapad models such as the [[Versafunction88 datapad|Versafunction88]].<ref name="NEGWT" /> Personal datapad assistant could manage electronic information through an interactive holographic heads-up display. <ref name="Dark Forces Jedi Knight">''[[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight]]''</ref>

[[Datacard/Legends|Datacards]] with specific information stored on them, such as [[Star map/Legends|star charts]], tourist guides, and works of fiction, were widely available. These datacards could be loaded into a datapad for easy access.<ref name="RPG-Core" /> Many planetary governments were legally obligated to provide such materials (especially regarding local laws) to all offworlders.

[[File:Star_Wars_RPG_Datapad.jpg|thumb|150px|Another type of datapad]]

Datapads were essential as note-taking devices. [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and the [[Meetra Surik|Jedi Exile]] frequently used their datapads to take notes and store information concerning their missions and tasks.

Some datapads could be rather sensitive; a datacard with dirt on its surface could ruin such a datapad's electronics.
[[File:Coronet_cargo_manifest.png|left|thumb|144x144px|A manifest of the cargo on the starship ''Coronet'']]
Some datapads designed for use in colder climates had oversized keys to ease key manipulation for users wearing [[thermal glove]]s.<ref name="Truce at Bakura Sourcebook">''[[The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Thanks to a stolen datapad, the primitive species known as [[Menahuun]] learned a lot about the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]]-level technology used by alien settlers.<ref name="R">{{GamerCite|7|Reckonings}}</ref>

==History==
[[Bounty hunter/Legends|Bounty hunters]] often used datapads to store mission information on their targets, locations, or other vitals. Personal datapads of this kind were designed to erase all stored information if not handled correctly.

[[Doctor/Legends|Doctors]] used a [[lightpad]] to monitor their patients' vitals<ref name="TCSWE">{{CSWECite|II|254|lightpad}}</ref> or most of the galactic [[Medcenter/Legends|hospitals]], including the [[Mah Dala Infirmary]], used a [[medical datapad]] to analysis and detection of diseases before they could act on the body of the infected [[Sentience/Legends|beings]]. 

[[Scout/Legends|Scouts]] used a [[survey datapad]] that was specially adapted to record survey data collected. This datapad had a flat [[Computer/Legends|computer]] that could be coupled to a special [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] array to record accurate geographical information as the scout moved across uncharted terrain by bouncing [[Electromagnet/Legends|electromagnetic]] rays off a [[Scout ship/Legends|scout vessel]] in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]]. The mapping features of the datapad were also uninterrupted by the scout using it to call up preloaded encyclopedic information.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 8 Scouts">''[[Galaxy Guide 8: Scouts]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In many [[LucasArts]] games, an on-screen datapad interface is used to show the game menu, which includes inventory, mission objectives, level maps, and other information.

[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'']] contains the earliest mention of datapads, though that book spelled the term "data pads."<ref name="Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game first edition">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'']] {{C|page 93}}</ref> The novel ''[[Heir to the Empire]]'' marks their first [[in-universe]] appearance. They are one of the [[List of Legends elements in the films|items that first appeared in the Expanded Universe that would later appear in the films]].
